# GEO report: quay-store

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. A cap of 40 applies, so the score is 40. The cap applies because GEO-009 has a blocker: `static/robots.txt:5` blocks Googlebot from the whole site.

This is a read-from-code result. Googlebot is told to stay out of every page, and the pages are built in the browser with no `lang` attribute. All of these can be fixed in a few small edits. Crawlers could still be affected by things outside the code, such as a CDN or firewall (see "Can't tell from code").

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot in robots.txt
- **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` tells Google's crawler to skip the whole site, including every page in your sitemap and menu.
- **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4-5`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small (delete the Googlebot group, so Googlebot follows the `*` group that allows everything)
- **Score after this:** 70/100. GEO-009 (3) and GEO-014 (3) become Clear, so earned is 18 ÷ 25 = 72 and the cap lifts. If this block is intentional, change your declared policy instead and expect the score to stay low.

### 2. Render page content on the server
- **Why it matters:** Many crawlers don't run JavaScript. With server rendering switched off, they receive an empty page shell for every route.
- **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;`
- **Size:** Small (remove the line, or set it to `true`, and check that nothing needs the browser at load time)
- **Score after this:** applied together with item 1, 21 ÷ 25 = 84. Alone, 15 ÷ 25 = 60, but the cap of 40 still holds until item 1 is done.

### 3. Add a language and fix descriptions
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines what language the site is in. A blank description gives them nothing to show for the page.
- **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` and `<meta name="description" content="" />`
- **Size:** Small (use `<html lang="en">`, and write a real description for /shop)
- **Score after this:** applied together with items 1 and 2, GEO-012 earns 2 and the score is 23 ÷ 25 = 92. Alone, 14 ÷ 25 = 56 before the cap, so 40 until item 1 is done.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt`: plain, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access you intend | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:5` `Disallow: /` for Googlebot. Assumed you want to be found |
| GEO-014 | Linked and sitemap routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/shop` are both blocked for Googlebot by `static/robots.txt:5` (0 of 2 routes clear) |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your own domain | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+page.svelte:4` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:4`. Domain taken from the sitemap and robots.txt |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` `export const ssr = false;`. `src/app.html:8` is an empty shell |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and has required properties | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`. The Product has only `name`; Google also requires `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating` |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is linked from robots.txt | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml`, `static/robots.txt:7` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang` (site-wide). `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` has an empty description |
| GEO-016 | Routes reachable through plain links | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5` uses `<a href>`. Whether the links reach the served HTML is covered under GEO-003 |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't fight AI search | Clear | Not run | No page-wide `nosnippet` and no header code. `+layout.svelte:7` `data-nosnippet` is a scoped choice |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and 3 pages. They have no images, and the links have text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app |

## Other problems found

None found. `/search` is `noindex` (`src/routes/search/+page.svelte:3`) and is not in the sitemap or menu, so that's consistent. It also has no description, but that doesn't matter for a noindexed page.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** the status codes and headers (such as `X-Robots-Tag`) that your host actually sends. A live scan would show them.
- **Crawlers beyond Googlebot:** `robots.txt` has no groups for `Bingbot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `Claude-SearchBot` or `PerplexityBot`. They fall under `*`, which allows everything. Only Googlebot is blocked.
- **GEO-004:** JSON-LD is also built at runtime inside `{@html …}`, so I read the literal string as written.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. There's no `geo.config.json`, so I assumed that goal.
- `https://quay.example` is your real origin. Robots, sitemap and canonicals all agree on it, but I couldn't confirm it.
- I sampled all three routes: `/`, `/shop` and `/search`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
